newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs end higher on rumours, Q3 GDP figures.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs end higher on rumours, Q3 GDP figures.

text.p: Shares ended Thursday's trading sharply higher as investment sentiment was boosted by market rumours of government boosting measures and better than expected third quarter gross domestic product figures, brokers said.
The composite stock index rose 14.30 points, or 1.98 percent, to a provisional close of 736.92. Advancers beat decliners 768 to 139, while volume slightly improved to 24.95 million shares.
"Rumours of market boosting measures and positive talks about next year's growth rate sent the index up," said a UBS Securities broker.

South Korea's GDP grew a real 6.4 percent in the third quarter against a 9.8 percent rise a year earlier. Brokers said this was better than expected by nervous investors, who had been anticipating a number just over six percent, they said.

A local market analyst said the market was rife with rumours that, among other measures, the government would allow pension funds to increase their investment in the bourse, by as much as a total of 800 billion won.
Blue chips were boosted in the late session by the rumours. Samsung Electronics jumped 2,200 won to 62,500, and Hyundai Motor gained 900 won to 24,500.
Small- and mid-cap shares which had caught the brunt of last week's selling rose throughout the day. Tae Heung Leather rose 100 won to 11,500. Sejin gained 600 won to 14,400.
Brokes said that if the boosting measures don't materialise, disappointed investors could spark another selling spree. They said the market was still under the shadow of share oversupply.
The government is selling 360 billion won of Korea Telecom shares on Thursday and Friday.
The December futures index also rose, gaining 1.60 points to 78.15, while the KOSPI 200 index climbed 1.30 points to 77.17.
